newsitem.title: UK: Sterling Eurobonds unmoved by UK government change.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Eurobonds unmoved by UK government change.

text.p: Sterling Eurobond traders were unruffled on Friday by Labour's landslide election victory and dealers said the sector was likely to remain steady throughout the day.

"If gilts and sterling continue (steady) as they are, not much will happen to Eurobonds. So far the market's reaction is fairly muted, although Labour's majority is larger than expected," a dealer at a British bank said.
"Japanese investors have not been playing Eurosterling spreads overnight, and we do not expect a reaction either way in Europe today," he said.
The BBC is forecasting a 181-seat Labour majority in Britain's parliament, bringing 18 years of Conservative rule to an abrupt end.
Sterling extended gains against the mark in the early hours of Friday, but was trading at 2.7934/44 marks at 0610 GMT, down from 2.7970/80 before polls results began.
British government bonds, which also saw an initial price surge, fell after heavy profit-taking and dealers expected further limited losses on Friday.
But the medium-term outlook for gilts was rosy, analysts said, with many putting their faith in Labour's finance minister-in-waiting Gordon Brown.

Brown said Labour, which has promised to deliver a budget within two months, would stick to a 2.5 percent annual inflation target. Markets have factored in a British interest rate rise of up to 50 basis points.
"Credit (Eurobond) spreads have been untested and so far unchanged," a Eurosterling dealer at another British bank said.

"Spreads will be secondary in people thoughts, so I don't imagine they will come under any pressure at all," he said, adding Japanese investors could resume buying of 10-year paper once British investors came to the market.
The sector's 10-year benchmark bond, a European Investment Bank (EIB) 7.625 percent 2007 bond, was trading at around 10 basis points over gilts at 0600 GMT, unchanged from Thursday's levels.
The five-year benchmark, a Fannie Mae 6.875 percent 2002 bond, was also unchanged at 11.5 b.p. over.
"The Japanese are waiting for the UK to enter the market. They were keen buyers of the ten-year sector on Thursday and are likely to remain so," a dealer said.
One key objective of Labour's budget will be to implement a windfall tax on privatised utilities.
Dealers said the market had factored in a three billion stg to five billion stg tax, and any level above that would hurt Eurobonds issued by British utilities.
"A lot of the bad news is already in utility spreads," a Eurosterling trader at a European bank said.
The sterling Eurobond sector has been buoyant in 1997, with foreign demand boosted by sterling's strength.
In the first quarter of this year, more than $26 billion equivalent of new bonds were launched, compared with $14 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
Dealers said primary market activity was likely to resume after the election, with the recent lull in issuance ahead of the election creating pent-up demand for sterling bonds.

Labour has pledged to continue public/private partnerships through the Private Finance Initiative (PFI), started up by the Conservative government to fund public infrastructure projects with private funds.
Deals in the pipeline include a two billion stg sell-off of the student loan portfolio and the sale of Department of Social Security office properties.
